Because bare peaks at -25 dBTP sat inside the old 30 dB knee, the bare and colour era hashes are re-baselined ONCE at Stage 2 with before/after inaudibility evidence rendered through the old tail and the new tail: (a) a pre-tail tap of bare-bed, colour-bed and crawl-to-ch1-fixed is fingerprint identical with every 16-bit sample delta at or under 2 LSB, proving the change is confined to the tail; (b) through the tail the same three renders hold integrated loudness within 0.3 LU, short-term loudness within 1 LU at every 3 s window and true peak within 0.5 dB of the old tail; (c) the owner (or the delegated production lead) A/Bs the bare and colour renders at the Stage 2 audition and hears no change; the new renders are then pinned as the bare-era before hash for Stage 3 onward. A story-floor check renders the ch4-defy, refused and seam-ebb hand-back excerpts through the old and new tails and holds each within 0.25 LU. Stage 2 measures the full music-path latency of the finished tail (today about 12 ms: the glue compressor's and the safety compressor's fixed look-aheads of about 6 ms each; a DynamicsCompressor-based limiter adds another) and publishes it as LATENCY_COMP_MUSIC_PATH_S for Stage 3.

contractAmendmentProposal.musicalRationale: A safety compressor at -20 dB / 8:1 with a 30 dB knee is a programme compressor: it acts on everything above -35 dBFS and turns the 6.5 LU BLOOM window the owner asked for into 2.3-3.4 LU (LRA 6.88 -> 3.26 corroborates). Once a true-peak limiter at -1 dBTP owns protection, the compressor's only legitimate job is to catch what the limiter's look-ahead cannot, so it moves up to -6 dB at 20:1 with a hard-ish knee and a fast attack, out of the programme's way. The Zimmer half of the brief lives in that window; the ODESZA half (sidechain breathing) is only audible if the tail stops flattening it. Retuning it twice (Stage 1 and again at Stage 2) would give the owner two audition deltas for one change, which is why it is a Stage 2 term and not a Stage 1 patch.
